evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/listing/ListingRepository.kt:46 — getListingDetail() splices listingId raw into the request path (client.get("$baseUrl/api/v1/listings/$listingId")) with no encodeURLPathPart(), whereas the sibling ApiClient.getListing (ApiClient.kt:84) deliberately routes the id through pathSegment()/encodeURLPathPart() to block path-injection. listingId flows from deep links (reality://listing/<id>) and nav args, so an id containing '/', '?', '#' or '..' can smuggle extra path segments/query params into the request. Inconsistent hardening; apply the same encoding here.

mobile-native/androidApp/src/main/java/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/navigation/Navigation.kt:440 and :458 — the MyListings and ListingAnalytics routes are wired into the production nav graph but render hardcoded listings=emptyList() / metrics=emptyList() with isLoading=false and no repository or ApiClient call. ApiClient exposes no my-listings or analytics endpoint at all, so both realtor screens are permanent empty stubs in production (distinct from the already-tracked CreateListing NotImplementedError stub). The realtor listing-management flow (create + list + analytics) is entirely unimplemented behind live navigation.
